pages.text: Cody the computer hums quietly on a desk. Inside him, tiny parts are ready to follow instructions.
Cody does not think on his own. He waits for people to give clear instructions called programs.
When a key is pressed or a mouse is clicked, Cody receives input. Input tells him something new.
Inside, Cody processes the information. Processing means working on the input step by step.
After processing, Cody shows results on the screen or plays a sound. This is called output.
Cody remembers things using storage. Storage keeps pictures, games, and documents safe inside.
Electric power keeps Cody awake. Without electricity, computers cannot run or respond.
Computers help people write stories, draw pictures, and learn new ideas every day.
Cody works best when instructions are clear. Good instructions help computers do the right job.
When the day ends, Cody rests. Tomorrow, he will follow new instructions and help again.
